ranked_facts.why: The presence of a milky white layer on the surface of the blood sample, indicative of hypertriglyceridemia, is more characteristic of lipoprotein lipase deficiency, a type of lipid storage disease, than glycogen storage disease, because it directly points to an issue with lipid metabolism rather than glycogen storage.

Hypertriglyceridemia causing lactescent plasma is a hallmark of lipoprotein lipase deficiency, which aligns more closely with the clinical presentation of lipid storage disease than glycogen storage disease, as it signifies a problem with the breakdown of triglycerides, a key aspect of lipid metabolism.
